\chapter{More Courtesy}
\label{ch:sa-courtesy-more}
\hlchaptermodality{37}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can wish someone peace, speak respectfully, call a host gracious, congratulate a friend and give a blessing in Sanskrit.}

Complete SA-C37-blessing and demonstrate the chapter promise.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[śāntiḥ]{\sk{शान्तिः} (śāntiḥ) — peace, stillness}

\label{lesson:SA-C37-peace}



\begin{quote}
Before the new word: what did \emph{samyak} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शान्तिः}}
\textbf{\sk{शान्तिः}} (\emph{śāntiḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}peace, stillness\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\sk{शान्तिः}} is peace of a particular kind: not the absence of war so much as the settling of something that had been disturbed. It comes from \emph{śam}, \textquotedblleft{}to grow calm, to come to rest\textquotedblright{}.

A great many Sanskrit texts close on it, said three times over, once for each of the troubles a person can meet. You already have \textbf{\sk{स्वस्ति}} for a wish of wellbeing; \textbf{\sk{शान्तिः}} is the quieter one, and the one you would say last.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for peace, and the way Sanskrit texts stop.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śāntiḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samyak}, then \emph{śāntiḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{dugdham}, then read \textbf{\sk{अपि}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{शान्तिः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}peace, stillness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sādaram]{\sk{सादरम्} (sādaram) — respectfully, with respect}

\label{lesson:SA-C37-respectfully}



\begin{quote}
Before the new word: what did \emph{śāntiḥ} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सादरम्}}
\textbf{\sk{सादरम्}} (\emph{sādaram}) — \textquotedblleft{}respectfully, with respect\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\sk{सादरम्}} is \emph{sa-}, \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}, joined to \emph{ādara}, \textquotedblleft{}regard, esteem\textquotedblright{} — so, \textquotedblleft{}with regard\textquotedblright{}.

It goes at the front of a request, where English would put its politeness at the end of a letter. Set beside \textbf{\sk{कृपया}} it makes a request about as courteous as Sanskrit gets: \emph{sādaram kṛpayā}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A politeness that goes at the front rather than the end.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sādaram}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śāntiḥ}, then \emph{sādaram kṛpayā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\sk{मधु}}, then say \emph{sarvam}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{सादरम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}respectfully, with respect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[prasannaḥ]{\sk{प्रसन्नः} (prasannaḥ) — pleased, gracious, clear}

\label{lesson:SA-C37-gracious}



\begin{quote}
Before the new word: what did \emph{sādaram} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{प्रसन्नः}}
\textbf{\sk{प्रसन्नः}} (\emph{prasannaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}pleased, gracious, clear\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\sk{प्रसन्नः}} describes a face that has cleared. The one word covers still water, a settled mind and a kindly host, because it is \emph{pra-}, \textquotedblleft{}forth\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{sad}, \textquotedblleft{}to settle\textquotedblright{}: what was cloudy has dropped its silt.

To say that a guest left you \textbf{\sk{प्रसन्नः}} is to say they left you at ease. The offering handed back from a temple, \emph{prasāda}, is this same word — grace, given a physical form.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for water, a mind and a host, all at once.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prasannaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sādaram}, then \emph{prasannaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{lavaṇam}, then read \textbf{\sk{तथा}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{प्रसन्नः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}pleased, gracious, clear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[abhinandanam]{\sk{अभिनन्दनम्} (abhinandanam) — congratulation, a greeting of delight}

\label{lesson:SA-C37-congratulations}



\begin{quote}
Before the new word: what did \emph{prasannaḥ} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अभिनन्दनम्}}
\textbf{\sk{अभिनन्दनम्}} (\emph{abhinandanam}) — \textquotedblleft{}congratulation, a greeting of delight\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\sk{अभिनन्दनम्}} is what you offer when something has gone well for somebody else. It is \emph{abhi}, \textquotedblleft{}towards\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{nand}, \textquotedblleft{}to rejoice\textquotedblright{} — gladness turned towards another person rather than kept.

That \emph{nand} is the piece inside \textbf{\sk{आनन्दः}}, the joy you met near the beginning of this book. The two words are the same delight, one held and one given away. Neuter \textbf{-\sk{अम्}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Joy from the beginning of this book, turned outwards towards somebody else.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ānandaḥ}, then \emph{abhinandanam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\sk{पुस्तकम्}}, then say \emph{mandam}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{अभिनन्दनम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}congratulation, a greeting of delight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āśīrvādaḥ]{\sk{आशीर्वादः} (āśīrvādaḥ) — a blessing}

\label{lesson:SA-C37-blessing}



\begin{quote}
Before the last word of the chapter: what did \emph{abhinandanam} mean, and what did \emph{śāntiḥ} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आशीर्वादः}}
\textbf{\sk{आशीर्वादः}} (\emph{āśīrvādaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a blessing\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\sk{आशीर्वादः}} is a blessing spoken aloud: \emph{āśis}, \textquotedblleft{}a wish, a prayer\textquotedblright{}, joined to \emph{vāda}, \textquotedblleft{}a speaking\textquotedblright{}.

That second piece is the one inside \textbf{\sk{धन्यवादः}}, the thanks you learned on your very first page — thanks is a speaking too. An elder gives \textbf{\sk{आशीर्वादः}}; you answer with \textbf{\sk{धन्यवादः}}; and the two are built the same way, out of a wish and a word for saying it.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five courtesies, and the piece shared by a blessing and a thanks.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āśīrvādaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} all five in order, then \emph{āśīrvādaḥ} and \emph{dhanyavādaḥ} together
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{śayyā}, then read \textbf{\sk{सम्यक्}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{आशीर्वादः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}a blessing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
